title: Formal glueing: the module H^0 of a glueing datum localizes to its components
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat ring map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $f_1,\dots,f_t\in R$. Let $\mathbf M=(M',(M_i)_i,(\alpha_i)_i,(\alpha_{ij})_{i,j})$ be an object of the category $\mathrm{Glue}(R\to S,f_1,\dots,f_t)$ of glueing data [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]: $M'$ an $S$-module, $M_i$ an $R_{f_i}$-module [def-weil-ring-localization-away], $\alpha_i:M'_{f_i}\to M_i\otimes_RS$ and $\alpha_{ij}:(M_i)_{f_j}\to(M_j)_{f_i}$ isomorphisms satisfying conditions (a) and (b) there; here $P_f$ is the localization of an $R$-module $P$ at $f$ with localization map $p\mapsto p/1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] and $P\otimes_RS$ the base change [def-weil-module-base-change]. Let $H^0(\mathbf M)$ be the $R$-submodule of $M'\times\prod_{i=1}^tM_i$ of the families $(m',(m_i)_i)$ with $\alpha_i(m'/1)=m_i\otimes1$ in $M_i\otimes_RS$ and $\alpha_{ij}(m_i/1)=m_j/1$ in $(M_j)_{f_i}$ for all $i,j$, and $p_i:H^0(\mathbf M)\to M_i$, $(m',(m_k)_k)\mapsto m_i$, the projection. Fix $i$. Then there is exactly one $R$-linear map $\pi_i:H^0(\mathbf M)_{f_i}\to M_i$ with $\pi_i(h/1)=p_i(h)$ for all $h\in H^0(\mathbf M)$, and $\pi_i$ is bijective.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition 05ER (proposition-equivalence, line 24813), second paragraph: the morphism Psi from Can(H^0(M)) to M becomes an isomorphism after the base change R -> R' = R_{f_i}, by combining Lemma 05EQ (lemma-base-change-glue, line 24792; H^0 commutes with the flat base change R -> R_{f_i}) and Lemma 05EP (lemma-equivalence-I-unit, line 24768; the case (f_1,...,f_t) = R, proved with Algebra Lemma 00EQ, lemma-glue-modules, algebra.tex line 4439). Stated here is the i-th module component of that isomorphism; H^0 is defined in Remark 05EL (remark-glueing-data, line 24641).

proof.text: Put $H=H^0(\mathbf M)$ and $u=f_i$. For each $j$ let $B_j=M_j\otimes_RS$ and $C_{jk}=(M_k)_{f_j}$. Define an $R$-linear map $d:M'\times\prod_jM_j\to\prod_jB_j\times\prod_{j,k}C_{jk}$ whose $j$-component is $\alpha_j(m'/1)-m_j\otimes1$ and whose $(j,k)$-component is $\alpha_{jk}(m_j/1)-m_k/1$. By the displayed definition of $H$ in the statement, $H=\ker d$ with its inclusion into the finite product. The maps and differences are $R$-linear because the localization and tensor maps are linear [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], [def-weil-module-base-change].

source.place: Remark 05EL (remark-glueing-data), displayed definition of H^0 and its exact sequence; Lemma 05EQ (lemma-base-change-glue)

proof.text: The natural map $H_u\to (M')_u\times\prod_j(M_j)_u$ identifies $H_u$ with the families satisfying the localized equations of step 1. Indeed localization at $u$ is exact [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so it preserves the kernel of $d$. Here localization commutes with the two finite products: a tuple of fractions has a common denominator $u^n$, obtained by taking the largest of its finitely many exponents, and a tuple is zero after localization precisely when one common power of $u$ kills every coordinate. Thus the localized map of $d$ is exactly the list of its component equations, localized at $u$. For surjectivity of the identification directly, write a compatible localized tuple with common denominator $u^n$; each of the finitely many equations becomes zero after multiplying by some power of $u$, so one common power $u^N$ clears them all. Its numerator multiplied by $u^N$ lies in $H$ and represents the original tuple as a fraction in $H_u$. The same common-power argument proves injectivity.

source.place: Lemma 05EQ (lemma-base-change-glue), proof omitted in the source; applied to localization at f_i as in the proof of Proposition 05ER (proposition-equivalence)

proof.text: For $x\in M_i$ construct a localized tuple $e(x)$. Its $M'$-coordinate is $y'=\alpha_i^{-1}(x\otimes1)\in(M')_u$; its $M_j$-coordinate is $y_j=\alpha_{ij}(x/1)\in(M_j)_u$ for every $j$. These expressions are meaningful because $u=f_i$ is invertible on $M_i$, $M_i\otimes_RS$, and $(M_j)_u$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]. The cocycle condition (b) with all three indices $i$ says $\alpha_{ii}^2=\alpha_{ii}$ after the canonical iterated-localization identifications; since $\alpha_{ii}$ is an isomorphism, it is the identity. Hence $y_i=x/1$, identified with $x$ under $(M_i)_u\cong M_i$. The tuple $e(x)$ is $R$-linear in $x$.

source.place: Lemma 05EP (lemma-equivalence-I-unit), proof: after a generator becomes a unit one component recovers the others; Remark 05EL, cocycle condition (b)

proof.text: The tuple $e(x)$ satisfies the localized equations of step 2. For the $j$th equation, localize condition (a) of [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data] at $u=f_i$ and evaluate it on $y'/1\in((M')_{f_i})_{f_j}$. Its left side, $(\alpha_{ij}\otimes_RS)c^{M_i}_{f_j}(\alpha_i)_{f_j}(y'/1)$, is $\alpha_{ij}(x/1)\otimes1=y_j\otimes1$; its right side, $c^{M_j}_{f_i}(\alpha_j)_{f_i}\sigma^{M'}_{f_i,f_j}(y'/1)$, is the image of $\alpha_j(y')$ under the tensor-localization identification. Hence the $j$th localized equation holds [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-canonical-maps] (2), (3). For the $(j,k)$th equation, evaluate condition (b) on $(x/1)/1$ in $((M_i)_{f_j})_{f_k}$ and localize at $u$: its left side is $\alpha_{jk}(y_j/1)$ and its right side is $y_k/1$ after the swaps $\sigma$ identify the iterated localizations [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-canonical-maps] (2). Thus step 2 supplies an element $e(x)\in H_u$ whose $i$th projection is $x$.

source.place: Remark 05EL (remark-glueing-data), conditions (a) and (b); Lemma 05EP (lemma-equivalence-I-unit); proof of Proposition 05ER (proposition-equivalence), second paragraph

proof.text: Conversely, let $(z',(z_j)_j)$ be a family in $H_u$ as described in step 2, and let $x=z_i\in(M_i)_u=M_i$. Its $i$th equation says $\alpha_i(z')=x\otimes1$, hence $z'=\alpha_i^{-1}(x\otimes1)=y'$. Its $(i,j)$th equation says $z_j=\alpha_{ij}(x/1)=y_j$ in $(M_j)_u$. Therefore the tuple equals $e(x)$, and the localized $i$th projection $H_u\to M_i$ and $e$ are inverse $R$-linear maps. The universal property of localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] says this projection is the unique $R$-linear map taking $h/1$ to $p_i(h)$; it is bijective as required.

split_report.summary: Split the localization of H0 into the finite equalizer calculation of Stacks 05EQ and the unit-component argument of 05EP used in the proof of 05ER. The source omits the details of 05EQ, so the proof clears common powers of f_i explicitly. Conditions (a) and (b) of the existing glueing-data node prove compatibility of the inverse tuple, and alpha_ii = id follows from its cocycle. Reused the existing Mathlib leaf localization-module-exact and existing formal-glueing-canonical-maps node; no new nodes or route changes. The flatness hypothesis is inherited from 05ER and is not needed for localization itself.

The five steps realize the equalizer, localization, inverse-tuple and compatibility calculations required there. Whole-blueprint searches for 05ER, formal glueing H0, and glueing localization found no duplicate statement.
